intro: Burkina Faso, meaning 'land of upright people', grew from the Mossi kingdoms and is known for its film festival and its revolutionary leader Thomas Sankara.

chapters.title: Mossi kingdoms
text: From around the 1400s the Mossi kingdoms, led by kings called the Mogho Naba, ruled the region and resisted the Mali and Songhai empires. The Mogho Naba still holds a ceremonial role in Ouagadougou.
The ruins of Loropéni, stone walls over 1,000 years old, are a World Heritage site.

chapters.title: Upper Volta
text: France conquered the region in the 1890s and later named it Upper Volta. It became independent in 1960.

chapters.title: Sankara and after
text: In 1983 Captain Thomas Sankara took power, renamed the country Burkina Faso, vaccinated millions of children and planted millions of trees. He was killed in a 1987 coup led by Blaise Compaoré, who ruled until protests forced him out in 2014.
Since 2015 attacks by armed Islamist groups have displaced millions. Captain Ibrahim Traoré seized power in 2022.
